chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: Whoever deals with people without oppressing them, speaks to them without lying to them, and makes promises to them without breaking them, is among those whose backbiting is prohibited, whose manliness (virtue) is complete, whose justice is evident, and brotherhood with him becomes obligatory.
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of a true believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni presents this hadith as a definitive criterion for the social integrity of the al-Mu'min, linking personal ethical conduct directly to communal rights. By ensuring justice, truthfulness, and promise-keeping, the believer secures the inviolability of their honor (hurmat ghaybatuhum) and establishes a binding bond of brotherhood (wujub ukhuwwatihum), reflecting the Shia emphasis on moral consistency as a sign of faith.
